fix: In the contract-gate correction path (orchestrator correction re-dispatch): on the SECOND consecutive contract block for the same phase attempt, re-dispatch on the profile's cli_fallback (or the universal claude fallback) instead of the same CLI, BEFORE burning the third strike that opens the circuit. Keep the circuit as the last resort. Emit a loud WARN naming the demoted phase + CLI when the circuit does open, and auto-file an inbox item (today the demotion is one log line and invisible in the cycle verdict). Regression test: fake CLI that always emits a contract-violating deliverable -> assert second correction goes to fallback CLI and the circuit does NOT open when the fallback complies.
notes: Console mitigation already applied 2026-07-29: .evolve/profiles/adversarial-review.json patched agy-tmux/balanced -> claude-tmux/deep (matches auditor/plan-reviewer/premise-challenge house pattern and the opus-class standing rule for adversarial work; batch-17 ran this phase on claude-tmux with zero contract blocks). The prompt template is NOT at fault — it names all required sections and the machine verdict line explicitly. | SECOND CONFIRMED INSTANCE 2026-07-30 (batch-21 cycle-1215): the SAME CLI (agy-tmux) failed the SAME sub-contract class on a DIFFERENT phase — triage emitted a v1 FAIL sentinel without the required schema_version-2 failure block, 3 blocks with both corrections exhausted, circuit demoting the contract gate on TRIAGE (more consequential than batch-19's adversarial-review: triage is the single-writer decision phase). Weight raised to 0.95. IMPORTANT SCOPING NOTE for the fix: do NOT simply reroute the phase — triage on agy has shipped many successful batches on the COMMON path (PASS + menu); the non-compliance is on the RARE FAIL+failure-block path, so a phase-wide reroute would change 99% of dispatches to fix 1%. That is precisely why per-correction CLI ESCALATION (this item) is the right shape: escalate only the re-dispatch that already failed the contract, leaving the common path untouched. ALTERNATIVE HYPOTHESIS to rule out first: the operator consumed an inbox item mid-flight (2026-07-30T13:0x, deliverable-verify-read-races-final-write) while this triage was reading the inbox — a claim-after-read race could contribute to a triage FAIL verdict. Check the cycle-1215 triage-report.md for a missing-item complaint before attributing the FAIL itself (the FORMAT violation is agy's regardless). | STRANDED CLAIM RELEASED 2026-07-30: this item sat in processing/cycle-1173 since batch-19 (that lane FAILed on the pre-cycleoutcome-seam binary, so nothing released the claim) — INVISIBLE to batch-20 and batch-21 triage the entire time, which is why the class recurred twice more while its fix sat unworked. The cycleoutcome seam now live (v22.11.1) closes the stranding class going forward.
summary: Batch-18 cycles 1171/1172: adversarial-review on agy-tmux failed its deliverable contract 7/7 times with byte-identical violations (missing '## Threat Model'/'## Findings', no parseable verdict) across correction re-dispatches in BOTH lanes. The contract-gate's correction loop re-dispatches to the SAME profile CLI; cli_fallback triggers only on infra exit codes [80 81 85 124 127], never on contract blocks. After 3 blocks the circuit opens and demotes enforce->advisory for the rest of the run — i.e. a CLI that systematically ignores the contract format silently WEAKENS the gate on every cycle it touches. The reports were substantive (real review, 'Verdict: PASS' in agy's own format) — this is a format-compliance failure class, not a review-quality failure class, and the escape hatch must be CLI escalation, not gate demotion.
title: Contract-gate corrections must escalate to the fallback CLI — re-dispatching the same non-compliant CLI converts enforce into advisory
